The first full-prune harness set the maximum one byte below the pre-compaction estimate. Ordinary compaction resolved the pressure without deleting roots, so the harness correctly rejected these runs. The revised threshold is half the fixture result-only estimate. The second harness required the coarse greedy planner to hit a one-byte target exactly; at width 4096 it legitimately left one result. The final checks match the public best-effort policy: triggered, below maximum, and removed roots equal the number of collected independent results. Rejected logs are retained and provide no performance claims.
